airport.name: Winnipeg / James Armstrong Richardson International Airport

summary: Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International Airport (YWG) is the busiest airport in Manitoba and the primary gateway to central Canada, located approximately 7 km west of downtown Winnipeg. Named after James Armstrong Richardson, a pioneering Canadian bush pilot and aviation entrepreneur who died in 1939, the airport serves as a key hub connecting the prairies with destinations across North America and internationally. It features a modern terminal complex handling over 4 million passengers annually.
faqs:
Q: How far is YWG from downtown Winnipeg?
A: The airport is located about 7 km (4.3 miles) west of downtown Winnipeg, with a typical drive time of 15-20 minutes depending on traffic.

Q: Does YWG have a main terminal or multiple terminals?
A: The airport operates a single main terminal building divided into two levels, with all arrivals and departures handled in this facility.

Q: Is YWG a hub for any major airline?
A: Yes, YWG serves as a hub for Calm Air and Perimeter Aviation, which provide extensive regional connectivity across Manitoba and northern Canada.

Q: Are there international flights from Winnipeg?
A: Yes, YWG offers direct flights to destinations in the United States, Mexico, the Caribbean, and select European destinations including seasonal service to London.
transport_tips: A taxi or rideshare from YWG to downtown Winnipeg typically costs around CAD $20-25 and takes 15-20 minutes. Winnipeg Transit Route 15 provides affordable bus service between the airport and downtown, operating throughout the day. Long-term and short-term parking options are available on-site, with shuttle services connecting remote lots to the terminal.
local_tip: If you have a long layover, consider taking a short taxi ride to Assiniboine Park or The Forks, two of Winnipeg's most popular attractions—both are within 15 minutes of the airport and offer a great way to stretch your legs between flights.
